title: Company priority lattice and ask portfolio (Q3 planning seed)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working seed for company-wide prioritization going into Q3 planning. The goal is to move from a long unordered backlog to a small portfolio of company-level asks with clear owners, hypotheses, and measurable signals. Use this doc to converge with execs and prepare the all-hands messaging and run-of-show.

TL;DR (one paragraph):
Pick a compact portfolio of 4–6 company bets for the quarter that together improve: a) infra economics (cost/token), b) latency SLO in top 3 regions, c) developer onboarding time, and d) enterprise readiness for Private. Each ask should have an owner, success metric, 6-week milestones, and a fallback if not ready. This seed lists candidate asks, risks, and suggested comms for the all-hands.

Priority lattice (quick notes / informal matrix):
- X axis: Value to customers (low -> high). Y axis: Time-to-impact (fast -> slow).
- Top-right quadrant (high value, fast impact):
  - Intelligent batching defaults for hosted API (owner: Priya Nair). Hypothesis: 10–15% per-token cost reduction for majority workloads within 6 weeks. Signal: median cost/token decreases by >=10% on pilot routes.
  - Developer quickstart templates (owner: Arjun Patel). Hypothesis: reduce first-successful-request time from median 20m -> 7m. Signal: region of interest new dev funnel completion rate +25%.
- High value, slow impact:
  - Private deployment automation (owner: Samir Ahmed). Big lift, will reduce seat time for Private customers and expand TAM. Signal: 2 pilot customers on automated VPC installs by EOW12.
- Lower value, fast:
  - Docs polish for model catalog (owner: Leah Torres) — low lift but helps adoption.

Candidate company asks (short cards):
1) Intelligent batching defaults (Priya)
   - Outcome: 10% unit cost reduction for common text gen routes.
   - 6-week cadence: experiment on 3 high-volume routes; deploy safe defaults; rollback guard rails.
   - Risks: regressions on latency for low-latency SLAs.
   - Dependencies: serving runtime kernel changes (INF-739), e2e telemetry in Console.

2) Developer quickstart + sample apps (Arjun)
   - Outcome: 50% increase in trial-conversion to paid within 14 days for API users.
   - 6-week cadence: publish 3 reference apps, one walkthrough video, embed snippets in onboarding flow.
   - Risks: maintenance burden for samples; attribution noise.

3) Private deployment installer + compliance checklist (Samir)
   - Outcome: reduce average deployment time from 6 weeks -> 2 weeks for enterprise.
   - 6-week cadence: GA installer v0.1 for AWS VPC, basic KMS integration.
   - Risks: infra edge-cases; legal review needed (linked: CON-588).

4) Console routing transparency and per-route SLOs (Leah)
   - Outcome: customers can pin routing policy and see per-request routing decisions.
   - 6-week cadence: expose routing logs for top 5 customers, add UI for pinning.
   - Risks: data sensitivity; storage cost.

Tradeoffs and rough prioritization heuristic:
- Prefer asks with clear revenue/retention linkage or outsized cost-savings.
- Avoid more than 2 heavy infra projects in same quarter unless paired with a dedicated Dedicated capacity budget.

All-hands: suggested run-of-show (15–20 minute company segment + breakouts):
- 0:00–0:90: CEO framing — why focus now (founders voice, 3 slides)
- 0:90–5:00: Product highlight — short demos of quickstart + batching pilot results (Arjun + Priya)
- 5:00–9:00: SRE & infra — risks and mitigations for Private automation (Samir)
- 9:00–12:00: Customer success — top asks from enterprise and draft roadmaps (Leah)
- 12:00–15:00: OKR ask and voting — present proposed 4 bets and open live poll (Miro poll)
- 15:00–20:00: Breakout Q&A by function (sales, eng, product, cs)
Notes: keep slides light; surface 1 risk per bet and a single ask for folks to act on next week.

Comms plan (pre/post all-hands):
- Pre: short 1-page primer (this doc condensed) + two internal threads: exec Q&A and engineering concerns. Owners: Maya (primer), Leah (Q&A).
- Post: publish one-pager to product docs, spin up OKR trackers in Confluence per bet, scheduled follow-ups at weeks 2 and 6.

Risk register (top known unknowns):
- Latency regressions from batching changes — mitigation: feature flag controlled rollout, synthetic canaries.
- Installer regressions across customer environments — mitigation: early pilot with one regional partner.
- Success metric attribution — mitigation: define primary signal ahead of rollout and instrument before launch.

Open questions for execs (to finalize before all-hands):
- Which of these do we treat as "SLA-backed" commitments vs "strategic experiments"? (impacts staffing and SLAs).
- Acceptable threshold for cost-savings before we declare success (is 7% enough or target 12%)?
- Level of transparency we want for routing logs to customers (PII and security tradeoffs).

Draft OKR seeds (language to iterate):
- Objective: Make inference predictable and economical for product teams.
  - KR1: Reduce median cost/token for hosted API by 10% on measured production routes.
  - KR2: Decrease median first-successful-request time for new developers from 20m -> 8m.
  - KR3: Deliver automated Private installer v0.1 and complete 2 pilot installs.

Action items (immediate next week):
- Priya: finalize experiment plan for batching and create telemetry dashboard (INF-739) — due 2026-03-17.
- Arjun: publish 3 quickstarts and link into onboarding flow; add tiny analytics ping to attribute conversion — due 2026-03-22.
- Samir: secure legal checklist signoff for KMS patterns and schedule pilot customer onboarding — due 2026-03-24.
- Leah: prepare 2 slide demo for console routing transparency and draft post-all-hands doc — due 2026-03-18.
- Maya: create one-pager and Miro poll for voting; set calendar invites for week-2 check-in — due 2026-03-15.

Loose notes and things to table:
- We should not finalize Dedicated capacity commitments until we see pilot telemetry from batching and from new autoscaling policies.
- Consider a small incentives program for pilot customers (discount/credits) to accelerate Private installs.
- Low-priority: migration of old docs into new docs site is ongoing but not required this quarter.

Questions for discussion in next leadership sync:
- Headcount tradeoffs to move two infra engineers to batching vs keep them on Private installer.
- Budget realism for enterprise pilots (expected spend vs runway).

References and quick links:
- INF-739 (kernel selection for batching)
- CS-412 (Private pilot backlog)
- Confluence: quarterly roadmap canvas

Draft status and how to use this doc:
- This is intentionally rough. Use it as the single source to converge questions and to prepare the all-hands two slides per bet. Update this doc with experiment owners' concrete signals before the all-hands.

End of seed draft.
